info.title: Stackportfolio API
info.description: Read and write your Stackportfolio profile and projects. Every request but this document needs an API key. Requests are rate limited per account, across all of its keys: 3 per second, 30 per minute, 300 per hour, 1000 per day.

post.summary: Add an image to a project
post.description: Optimises the image server-side and appends it to the project's gallery; the first image becomes the cover. Takes a JSON body with base64 `data`, or multipart/form-data with a `file` part and an optional `description`. The decoded image may be at most 5 MB. A project holds a limited number of images set by its owner's plan; one more is a 409. Only an accepted OWNER or MAINTAINER may write; anyone else gets the same 404 as for a missing project.

data.description: The image, base64-encoded (a data: URL is accepted). PNG, JPEG, WebP or a still GIF; at most 6 MB of base64 in a JSON body. It is resized to at most 2048px, converted to WebP and stripped of metadata. The REST endpoint also takes multipart/form-data with the file in a `file` field.

description.description: Caption and alt text for the image.

file.description: The image file; at most 5 MB.

description.description: Caption and alt text for the image.

post.summary: Create a single-use upload URL for a project image
post.description: Generates a short-lived (10 min), single-use HMAC-signed PUT URL to upload a project image directly without base64 encoding. Accepts PNG, JPEG, or WebP up to 5 MB. Only an accepted OWNER or MAINTAINER may write; anyone else gets the same 404 as for a missing project.

filename.description: Original filename for the image, including extension.

contentType.description: The MIME type of the image to upload (image/png, image/jpeg, or image/webp).

description.description: Caption and alt text for the image.

altText.description: Alt text for the image (defaults to description if omitted).

201.description: The signed upload URL and required headers.

RateLimit-Limit.description: The request allowance of the window closest to running out.

put.summary: Upload an image to a signed URL
put.description: Authorised by the signed URL alone, no key. The body is the raw PNG, JPEG or WebP bytes (not multipart) with the Content-Type from createProjectMediaUpload, at most 5 MB. The URL works once and expires after 10 minutes; a used URL is a 409, an expired one a 410, an oversized body a 413. Responds with the stored image.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The signed token from the upload URL.

patch.description: Updates metadata (caption, alt text), position/sort order, or cover status for a media item. Only an accepted OWNER or MAINTAINER may write; anyone else gets the same 404 as for a missing project.

altText.description: Alt text for the image; null clears it.

makeCover.description: Whether this media item should become the project cover.

put.description: Replaces the image file with a new upload (base64 data or multipart file). Optimises to WebP with responsive variants and deletes the old stored objects. Only an accepted OWNER or MAINTAINER may write; anyone else gets the same 404 as for a missing project.

data.description: The replacement image, base64-encoded. At most 6 MB of base64; data: URL accepted.

description.description: Optional caption and alt text for the replacement image.

file.description: The replacement image file; at most 5 MB.

description.description: Optional caption and alt text for the replacement image.

delete.description: Deletes the media item and its stored files (including variants), repairing cover and position ordering. Only an accepted OWNER or MAINTAINER may write; anyone else gets the same 404 as for a missing project.

patch.summary: Update a technology on a project
patch.description: Marks a technology former (moved off), optionally naming the technology that replaced it. Send only the keys to change. A former technology still counts for proficiency, so nobody is rescored. A technology the project does not list and a project the caller may not edit are the same 404. Only an accepted OWNER or MAINTAINER may write; anyone else gets the same 404 as for a missing project.

anyOf.description: The major or major.minor version the project used, like "5" or "3.12"; null when unknown.

version.description: The version to set; null or "" clears it.

former.description: Whether the project moved off this technology.

replacedBy.description: The id of the technology that replaced it, which the project must list and which must not be this one. Needs former: true; null clears it, as does former: false.

delete.description: Deletes the evidence it gave on this project and rescores its contributors. Only an accepted OWNER or MAINTAINER may write; anyone else gets the same 404 as for a missing project.

put.summary: Set which technologies a contributor used
put.description: Replaces one accepted contributor's technology credits on this project and rescores them; proficiency stays computed. The caller may set their own, and an accepted OWNER or MAINTAINER anyone's but the owner's. A pending invitee, a target the caller may not change, and a project the caller is not on are the same 404.

technologyIds.description: The whole set, replacing the current one. Each must be one of the project's technologies.

put.summary: Set the skills a contributor used
put.description: Replaces the caller's own skills on this project and recomputes their skill levels. `userId` must be the caller: nobody records skills for someone else, and any other id is a 404.

skills.description: The whole list, replacing the current one. At most 10, each at most 50 characters; repeats are dropped case-insensitively.

get.description: Every "How I worked on this" account written on the project, as its page renders them. `mine` keeps only the caller’s own.

get.description: One contributor's story on a project the caller may see. Any author's story is readable, as the project page renders it; pass the caller's own id from `/me` to read theirs.

RateLimit-Limit.description: The request allowance of the window closest to running out.

put.description: Writes the caller’s own "How I worked on this" account, replacing any previous one. Every accepted contributor may write theirs, and nobody — owner included — may write anybody else’s: a project the caller is not on and a missing one are the same 404. Declaring a practice makes `corrections` mandatory, which is the anti-AI-washing rule the web editor enforces.

delete.description: Deletes the caller’s own story on the project. The contribution itself is untouched: only the write-up goes. Only ever the caller’s own story, so `projects:write` is enough.
